issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: USB CDC HardFault is USB is not connected
Context: repo=STM32CubeF1, mcu_series=None, board=STM32F411, component=USB, layer=Middleware, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=73
Root cause: Hello @nickshl, Thank you for your report.
Fix: When I work on one of my project based on STM32F411, I used this code to send data over USB: // Send to USB if(USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer(&hUsbDeviceFS, usb_data, rx_usb_cnt) == USBD_OK) { // Send packet - no waiting USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket(&hUsbDeviceFS); } And it works just fine regardless if USB is connected or not.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: STM32F411, Middleware, USB, bug_report, high, bug, wontfix, spotted before customer, st usb, USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer, usb_data, rx_usb_cnt

Technical details:
When I work on one of my project based on STM32F411, I used this code to send data over USB: // Send to USB if(USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer(&hUsbDeviceFS, usb_data, rx_usb_cnt) == USBD_OK) { // Send packet - no waiting USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket(&hUsbDeviceFS); } And it works just fine regardless if USB is connected or not. When I tried use the same code on STM32F103 MCU, exactly the same code caused HardFault. Turns out that it happens because function USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer() slightly different. This is how this function looks like for F103 MCU: uint8_t USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer(USBD_HandleTypeDef *pdev, uint8_t *pbuff, uint16_t length) { USBD_CDC_HandleTypeDef *hcdc = (USBD_CDC_HandleTypeDef *) pdev->pClassData; hcdc->TxBuffer = pbuff; hcdc->TxLength = length; return USBD_OK; } And this is how it looks like for F411 MCU: uint8_t USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer(USBD_HandleTypeDef *pdev, uint8_t *pbuff, uint32_t length) { USBD_CDC_HandleTypeDef *hcdc = (USBD_CDC_HandleTypeDef *)pdev->pClassDataCmsit[pdev->classId]; if (hcdc == NULL) { return (uint8_t)USBD_FAIL; } hcdc->TxBuffer = pbuff; hcdc->TxLength = length; return (uint8_t)USBD_OK; } As you can see, USB CDC for F411 MCU have null pointer check and return an error. As result this function can be safely called regardless in USB is connected and enumerated or not. Probably the same null pointer check should be included for F1 MCUs.

Key comments:
Hello @nickshl, Thank you for your report. We are aware of this point. Currently, STM32CubeF1 still supports an old version of the USB Device library, and its upgrade is planned for an upcoming release. We will keep you informed. BR, Mohamed. Hello @nickshl, Currently, STM32CubeF1 still supports an old version of the USB Device library. BR, Mohamed Chaker.

issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: SET_BIT, CLEAR_BIT and MODIFY_REG are not atomic
Context: repo=STM32CubeF1, mcu_series=None, board=None, component=UART, layer=Other, issue_kind=usage_question, severity=medium, evidence_strength=medium, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=67
Root cause: Hello @IvanSojic, First of all, please excuse this late reply.
Fix: In systems using RTOS, functions SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT are not atomic.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: UART, usage_question, medium, question, rtos, SET_BIT, CLEAR_BIT, HAL, ATOMIC_SET_BIT, ATOMIC_CLEAR_BIT

Technical details:
In systems using RTOS, functions SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT are not atomic. Since many macros from LL and HAL level are using SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT functions, What is general recommendation in systems with RTOS? We have also noticed implementation of ATOMIC_SET_BIT, ATOMIC_CLEAR_BIT, etc. What is their intention, since they are mostly used only for UART driver? Best regards, Ivan Sojic

Key comments:
Hello @IvanSojic, First of all, please excuse this late reply. 1. SET_BIT and CLEAR_BIT macros are indeed not atomic 2. In case of RTOS usage, it is customer application responsibility to manage the protection of shared resources by the different threads (via mutex). 3. ATOMIC_SET_BIT and ATOMIC_CLEAR_BIT macros were introduced to handle the specific case where parallel processes in bare metal implementation may need to access the same register for interrupt control; this is the case of UART driver where you can run in parallel Rx & TX processes and all interrupts are being handle in CR1/CR3 registers causing side effects if accesses are not atomic. I hope this answers your question. Please allow me to close this issue.

Fix: **Describe the set-up** STM32CubeIDE Version: 1.

Keywords: HAL, UART, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, cube mx, tim, UTC, STM32, RC4, SYS

Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** STM32CubeIDE Version: 1.9.0 Build: 12015_20220302_0855 (UTC) which uses STM32CubeMX - STM32 Device Configuration Tool Version: 6.5.0-RC4 Build: 20220225-1913 (UTC) Copyright (c) 2022 STMicroelectronics. All rights reserved **Describe the bug** Moving the SYS timebase to a timer that was previously configured for something elese, but then disabled will cause an invalid configuration where the timer IRQs are not generated. **How To Reproduce** Issue is exclusive to the STM32CubeIDE Device Configuration Tool / STM32CubeMX code generation. It is reproducible with an empty project. - start with a fresh project on F1 platform, for example STM32F103RG MCU ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/22d6c311-b1dc-4e50-8b72-195ddc4d1da2) ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/b6d6cfed-e1e5-4bee-bf5a-0ffec83954fb) - generate code using defaults - configure free timer (eg. TIM6, will be used for the rest of this example) for HAL timebase, generate code ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/a6cbdeac-bb20-4e41-b833-c039eff86cda) - revert HAL back to systick, generate code ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/1def6ff7-c558-4f6d-89d7-ff37311fb269) - manually configure the timer (TIM6), enable interrupts, generate code ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/e684e406-e037-430f-b1ee-e21ce08214d1) ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/10e9f62d-69ed-4568-bf57-1093bbf45bab) As it was previously used for HAL, the timer gets configured with an interrupt priority of 15 (**this is also a bug**) ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/3b605a13-63fc-4cdf-85ba-c87e6052e773) - disable the timer (TIM6), reuse it for HAL timebase source again, generate code ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/fe4ce3b3-8fc8-4539-8075-63719f7704fd) ![image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/assets/106665537/44e42515-2dc1-4f8a-ba5c-a3aa22b10af8) This will generate the stm32f1x_hal_timebase_tim.c, configured for the timer (TIM6), but its IRQ Handlers will get removed, causing the platform to hang in Default_Handler at start. Notably, the following configuration line will be missing NVIC.TIM6_IRQn=true\:15\:0\:false\:false\:true\:false\:true\:true One can recover from this configuration by - reverting HAL to SysTick - closing the Device Configuration Tool and reopening it back again - configuring HAL to that timer Closing and reopening also seems to mitigate the interrupt priority assignment when manually configuring the timer, it will be configured as other devices (in a fresh project it should be 5). I could not reproduce it with the above procedure, but such changes may also cause the change of TICK_INT_PRIORITY **Additional context** There are some other related bugs - https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-mcus/value-of-tick-int-priority-default-value-changed/td-p/136027 - https://community.st.com/t5/stm32cubeide-mcus/tick-int-priority-affected-by-enabling-trace-outputs/m-p/588892/highlight/true#M20524

The current MMC HAL driver fails to init due to not selecting the card before attempting to read the extended CSD register. Technical details:
**Describe the set-up** Tested with STM32F103C8T6. Same code can be found for F0 series and others. **Describe the bug** Usually, the procedure to return control to the host after a handled SETUP packet in USB is done by receiving 0 byte on the OUT control endpoint. For PMA assisted chips this results in a) an interrupt which confirms the finished receive operation followed by b) an interrupt for the next SETUP packet. In case it takes quite long to handle the a) interrupt (due to low interrupt priority for example) the length information of the SETUP packet will be overwritten. This is the relevant part from the code: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/blob/6ead386a08dea17f4dffbdbcd36c9979cb53588b/Drivers/STM32F1xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f1xx_hal_pcd.c#L2130-L2174 The situation was already improved in 1.8.0 by avoiding the call of the user callback function in case of such an a) interrupt (see line 2157). However, the root issue remains and can lead to a race condition were a SETUP packet is received just between line 2152 and 2172 and the received byte count being overwritten in line 2172. This behavior can be proven by checking (PCD_GET_ENDPOINT(hpcd->Instance, PCD_ENDP0) & USB_EP_SETUP) != 0 at line 2171. I suggest to properly re-check the USB_EP_SETUP bit and avoid PCD_SET_EP_RX_CNT() and PCD_SET_EP_RX_STATUS() if set.

Hello STMicroelectronics, Great libraries and support all over the Internet. I'm looking for EEPROM Emulation for my STM32 BluePill, And found the official documentation for that (AM2594) Which is a great document and well documented library. Anyway I'm planning to use more than 2 pages to store my rapid changing variable. So started to reverse engineer the existing library to write a more general library (independent of # of pages). While reverse Engineering : I found this [little line ](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF1/blob/441b2cbdc25aa50437a59c4bffe22b88e78942c9/Projects/STM32F103RB-Nucleo/Applications/EEPROM/EEPROM_Emulation/Src/eeprom.c#L312) that I can't understand as 'sensible' line : It's in a routine for checking whether the page is fully erased or not. While it compares the address passed with a **Fixed defined Address** PAGE0_END_ADDRESS. So when the address passed is PAGE1_BASE_ADDRESS it would definitely fail! As PAGE1_BASE_ADDRESS is greater than PAGE0_END_ADDRESS. Proposed solution to solve this issue is (whole function) : cpp uint16_t EE_VerifyPageFullyErased(uint32_t Address) { uint32_t readstatus = 1; uint16_t addressvalue = 0x5555; uint32_t endAddress = Address + (PAGE_SIZE - 1); /* Check each active page address starting from end */ while (Address <= endAddress) { /* Get the current location content to be compared with virtual address */ addressvalue = (*(__IO uint16_t*)Address); /* Compare the read address with the virtual address */ if (addressvalue != ERASED) { /* In case variable value is read, reset readstatus flag */ readstatus = 0; break; } /* Next address location */ Address = Address + 4; } /* Return readstatus value: (0: Page not erased, 1: Page erased) */ return readstatus; } Thank you!
